record.question:
Each EC2 application instance has a separate 120 GiB io1 EBS data volume provisioned for 3,000 IOPS. The application needs persistent block storage, not a shared network file system. Production-workload tests on a 120 GiB gp3 volume at 3,000 IOPS and 125 MiB/s meet the application's latency, throughput, and durability requirements. The EC2 instances have sufficient EBS bandwidth.

Which change removes unnecessary storage and provisioned-performance expense while preserving the tested requirements?

options.text: Replace each data volume with an Amazon EFS file system and access it through NFS.
Change each data volume to 120 GiB gp3 with its included baseline of 3,000 IOPS and 125 MiB/s.
Change each data volume to a 1 TiB gp2 volume to obtain slightly more than 3,000 baseline IOPS.
Move the data to EC2 instance store volumes and recreate them whenever an instance is replaced.

explanation.text:
<<2>> is correct. gp3 includes 3,000 IOPS and 125 MiB/s independently of volume size. The stated test establishes that this baseline meets the workload's needs, so additional performance provisioning and extra capacity are unnecessary.

<<1>> changes the required storage interface from block storage to a network file system.

<<3>> couples performance to unnecessary capacity. gp2 baseline IOPS scale at 3 IOPS per GiB, so 1,024 GiB provides 3,072 baseline IOPS, but the application needs only 120 GiB.

<<4>> does not preserve the required data lifecycle. Instance store data does not persist through instance stop or termination.

IOPS and throughput are different constraints: IOPS counts operations per second, while MiB/s measures bytes transferred. The conclusion depends on measured latency, throughput, durability needs, and instance limits, not matching an IOPS number alone.

Official AWS references (checked September 18, 2026): [General Purpose SSD volumes](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/ebs/latest/userguide/general-purpose.html). [EC2 instance store persistence](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/instance-store-lifetime.html).

diagram_alt: A comparison separates storage capacity from baseline IOPS and identifies the gp3 configuration already validated by workload testing.

sources.supports: gp3 included baseline independent of capacity and gp2 baseline IOPS per GiB
Temporary block storage and data persistence limits

editorial_notes: Preserved answer 2 and the existing repaired workload test; retained separate latency, throughput, persistence, and durability constraints.
